Consumer stocks were mixed late Monday afternoon, with the State Street Consumer Staples Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLP) down 0.2% and the State Street Consumer Discretionary Select Sector SPDR ETF (XLY) rising 1.9%.

In corporate news, Unilever (UL) has agreed to sell first-aid and bandage brand Welly Health to Forward Consumer Partners, the companies confirmed Monday. Unilever shares were down 1.6%.

Walmart (WMT) is poised to raise at least $6 billion from its sale of US and Canadian dollar bonds, Bloomberg reported. The retail giant has commenced an offering of at least C$4.25 billion ($3 billion) of Canadian notes, as well as a $3 billion offering of US dollar bonds, the report said. Walmart shares were fractionally higher.

Silgan (SLGN) and American Industrial Partners will acquire Dutch metal packaging products manufacturer Trivium Packaging, creating a $7.3 billion global metal packaging supplier for the food and beverage markets. Silgan shares jumped 6%.

Tesla (TSLA) said in a regulatory filing that it has nominated Elon Musk, Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel for a re-election to the board at its Dec. 3 annual meeting. The filing showed Musk's total compensation for 2025 was about $158.4 billion. Tesla shares rose 4%.

title: Walmart sells US debt, eyes Canadian market as spending grows
detail:
Walmart sells US debt, eyes Canadian market as spending grows
1 / 1
Walmart sells US debt, eyes Canadian market as spending grows
A worker stocks the shelves at a Walmart store in Victoria, British Columbia.
Brian Smith and Chunzi Xu
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 10:36 AM CDT 3 min read
WMT
DX-Y.NYB
Trade Walmart on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

(Bloomberg) -- Walmart Inc. is selling US dollar bonds for a second time this year and sounding out investors for a debut Canadian debt offering as the world's largest retailer seeks to diversify its funding sources amid a spending spree.

Most Read from Bloomberg

Zelenskyy Says Trump Is Pushing Ukraine, Not Putin, to Yield

Musk Says He'll Gift SpaceX Shares to 'Every Kid in America'

White House Turmoil Erupts as Trump Axes Zacharia, Backs Wiles

Nasdaq 100 Climbs on AI Trade Revival After Rout: Markets Wrap

Sydney's New $4 Billion Airport Opens With Barely Any Flights

The company is seeking to raise at least $2.5 billion through a four-tranche US dollar bond offering on Monday, with maturities ranging from three to 10 years, according to people familiar with the matter. Initial price talk on the longest tenor is a yield premium of 0.75 percentage point over Treasuries, the people added, asking not to be identified because they're not authorized to speak publicly.

Walmart has also asked Bank of America Corp., Bank of Nova Scotia and Toronto-Dominion Bank to hold investor calls on a potential debt offering in Canadian dollars, separate people said. The firm is mulling raising at least C$3.5 billion ($2.5 billion) in the deal, which would comprise four tranches spanning four to 30 years, though no final decision has been made on the transaction's size, they added.

Walmart has boosted investments over the past few years as part of a plan to add new stores, expand its e-commerce capabilities and automate some tasks, with the company expected to spend a record $29 billion next year, according to analyst estimates compiled by Bloomberg. The retailer also has about $3.3 billion of bonds maturing next year.

With the debut Canadian-dollar debt offering, the $940 billion company is following in the footsteps of US technology giants Alphabet Inc. and Amazon.com, which have also tapped the market this year to fund their artificial intelligence infrastructure investments. The Canadian bond market offers currency and investor diversification for US borrowers, while local investors have snapped up debt sold by foreign firms to broaden their exposure across sectors and issuers.

The shorter-dated bonds are being discussed at spreads as much as four basis points wider than comparable bonds of Ontario utility Hydro One Ltd, while the longest maturity is expected to price as much as seven points tighter, the people said.

Walmart - which typically sells bonds just once a year — last tapped the US market in April, when it raised $4.25 billion.

title: WMT, TGT & DG Bet Big on Capital Spending to Drive Next Growth Wave
detail:
WMT, TGT & DG Bet Big on Capital Spending to Drive Next Growth Wave
Sumit Singh
Mon, October 19, 2026 at 7:15 AM CDT 3 min read
WMT
TGT
DG
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Major U.S. retailers are stepping up capital expenditures to strengthen their store networks, modernize supply chains and improve technology capabilities. Investments in new stores, remodels, automation and digital infrastructure remain important as retailers seek to enhance customer convenience, improve operational efficiency and support long-term growth. Walmart Inc. WMT, Target Corporation TGT and Dollar General Corporation DG are directing capital toward these priorities.

Walmart Prioritizes Automation and Supply-Chain Investments

Walmart has increased its capital expenditure outlook for fiscal 2027 to about 4% of annual net sales from its prior expectation of 3.5%. The company continues to invest in infrastructure and capabilities supporting its evolving omnichannel retail model.

The retailer's investments in supply-chain automation, technology, fulfillment capacity and its physical network are helping improve inventory movement, product availability and delivery speed. These capabilities support its growing e-commerce and marketplace operations while strengthening efficiency across its distribution network.

Walmart's global e-commerce sales increased 23% in the second quarter of fiscal 2027, highlighting the importance of its digital and fulfillment capabilities. Despite higher planned capital spending, management expects double-digit free cash flow growth for the fiscal year. This suggests continued emphasis on balancing infrastructure investments with cash generation.

Target Expands Store and Technology Investments

Target is accelerating capital investments to strengthen its physical footprint, supply chain and technology infrastructure. The company expects approximately $5 billion in capital expenditures for fiscal 2026, supporting its strategic growth priorities.

Through the first half of 2026, Target deployed approximately $2.4 billion in capital expenditures, up nearly 30% year over year. Spending has focused on new stores, full-store remodels, supply-chain improvements and technology capabilities. Target opened 17 new stores during the second quarter, bringing its first-half total to 24. 

Target is also modernizing technology to improve personalization, strengthen digital engagement and enhance operational execution. These initiatives complement its broader strategy of delivering differentiated merchandise, convenience and value to customers.

Dollar General Focuses on Store Growth and Remodels

Dollar General is maintaining its capital expenditure outlook of $1.4 billion to $1.5 billion for fiscal 2026. During the first half, the company invested approximately $758 million, including $414 million in existing-store improvements, upgrades, remodels and relocations.

Another $168 million supported distribution and transportation projects, while $133 million was allocated to new-store facilities. Technology-related investments totaled approximately $31 million.

Dollar General plans approximately 4,730 real estate projects in fiscal 2026, including new-store openings, relocations and remodels under Project Renovate and Project Elevate. These projects aim to improve store presentation, customer experience and operational efficiency.

title: Management Raised The Bar For CVS Health Stock; Does The Chart Agree?
detail:
Management Raised The Bar For CVS Health Stock; Does The Chart Agree?

^GSPC

Trading disclosure
Image from Pixabay

On August 5, 2026, CVS Health (CVS) management raised its fiscal 2026 revenue forecast to at least $414 billion, up from $405 billion in May. Yet the stock has fallen 11.5% since the close prior to that release, compared with a 1.0% dip for the S&P 500. When a higher financial outlook meets a declining share price, investors should examine the technicals before taking the new numbers at face value. So does the CVS Health chart agree with the raise?

Partly: CVS Health Shares Fell But Trade Above Averages

The stock still trades above its key moving averages. CVS Health closed at $92.36 on October 16. That lands just above its 50-day average of $91.73, which tracks the closing price over the last 50 trading days. In turn, that figure sits above the 200-day average of $87.51, representing the average close across the last 200 trading days.

However, the return since the forecast update points the other way. The stock fell 7.9% in the two sessions around the release, while the S&P 500 slipped 0.3%. That market reaction priced the latest quarterly results and the new guide together. The shares then lost another 4.0% through October 16, underperforming a 0.7% dip for the broader index.

What CVS Health Management Raised For Fiscal 2026

The company upgraded its profit and cash targets as well. Management now expects adjusted EPS, an earnings measure the company defines itself, to land between $7.90 and $8.10. That is up from a prior target of $7.40, at the mid-point of the range. The company also projects cash flow from operations, the money generated by daily business activities, will reach at least $11.5 billion, compared with $9.5 billion previously. Executives credited this revision to strong performance so far in fiscal 2026. Furthermore, management noted that each operating segment grew earnings during the quarter ended June.

Part of that strength originated outside the three-month period itself. Management said items tied to earlier plan years contributed about $500 million, or 1.4 percentage points, to the medical benefit ratio. This metric tracks the share of premiums spent on medical care. The company also noted that some value initially expected in the second half of the year arrived early.

What Must CVS Health Deliver Before Fiscal 2026 Ends?

The short answer is less than it delivered a year ago. The higher forecast leaves about $207 billion of revenue to be recognized across the quarters ending September and December. That implies a figure about 0.5% less than CVS Health reported for the same two quarters of fiscal 2025. Revenue during the first half of the year grew 6.7% from a year earlier, so the updated guidance allows second-half revenue to slip below last year's pace.

title: Amazon.com vs. Walmart: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Amazon.com vs. Walmart: Which Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jack Delaney, The Motley Fool
Sun, October 18, 2026 at 10:20 PM CDT 5 min read
AMZN
WMT
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Is the digital cloud giant or the global retail king a better fit for your portfolio? Deciding between Amazon (NASDAQ:AMZN) and Walmart (NASDAQ:WMT) requires weighing high-growth tech against steady brick-and-mortar stability.

Amazon leads in e-commerce and cloud computing, while Walmart dominates the physical retail landscape with its massive grocery presence. Both companies are now blurring these lines, competing fiercely in online delivery and advertising. Understanding their different financial profiles is essential for deciding which path suits your investment goals in 2026.

The case for Amazon

Amazon operates a diverse business ecosystem, including online stores, third-party seller services, and an advertising platform. Its powerful Amazon Web Services segment provides cloud infrastructure and machine learning capabilities to enterprises, while the company also manages a $309.5 million class action settlement involving customer refunds. Navigating these complexities is central to managing a global workforce of 1.5 million employees among retail stocks.

In the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, according to its latest annual report, revenue reached nearly $716.9 billion, representing a growth of approximately 12.4% compared with the prior fiscal year. This expansion was accompanied by a net income of roughly $77.7 billion.

Amazon has total cash of $122.9 billion against total debt of $251.6 billion. It also has a total debt-to-equity ratio of 45.6%, and its 12-month trailing operating cash flow is $161.4 billion.

The case for Walmart

Walmart serves approximately 280 million customers weekly through a vast network of physical stores and an expanding e-commerce presence. The company is currently integrating AI and supply chain automation to improve its omnichannel strategy. It also offers financial services by collaborating with partners like Mastercard (NYSE:MA) to provide credit cards to its members.

In the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, as reported in its most recent annual filing, revenue reached close to $713.2 billion, a 4.7% increase year over year. The majority of these net sales were generated by the company's domestic Walmart U.S. and Sam's Club U.S. operations. For this period, the company reported net income of approximately $21.9 billion.

Walmart has total cash of $11.5 billion compared to total debt of $75 billion. Its total debt-to-equity ratio is 71.6%, and its 12-month trailing operating cash flow is $42.9 billion.

Risk profile comparison

Amazon.com faces intense global competition across retail, advertising, and cloud services where rivals often possess localized advantages or greater resources. International operations in regions like China and India carry risks of regulatory and ownership constraints that could disrupt the business model. Additionally, the company manages significant legal challenges including antitrust proceedings from the Federal Trade Commission and risks related to its complex global fulfillment networks.
